newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Kuala Lumpur bourse mulls shorter settlement time.
newsitem.headline: Kuala Lumpur bourse mulls shorter settlement time.

text.p: The Kuala Lumpur Stock Exchange (KLSE) is asking stockbroking firms in Malaysia for feedback on a proposal to shorten the time period for stock transaction settlements to three trading days from five.
In a circular sent to brokers dated August 28, the KLSE said it was considering the need to move to T+3 (transaction plus three days) from the current T+5.

A copy of the circular, obtained by Reuters, says the main objectives for the shorter settlement include minimising counterparty risk and market exposure and bringing Malaysia more in line with settlement time frames in other markets.
For example, the United States, Japan and France all practice T+3, while T+2 settlement is done in Hong Kong, Germany, South Korea and Taiwan.

"Shorter settlement period reduces the time during which one party is exposed to the other and thus the time during which one party could fail and the time during which the market price could move in an unfavourable direction," the KLSE letter said.

The exchange said it was seeking views on issues including the ability of retail investors to deliver monies for a purchase as well as the ability of institutional investors to deliver shares for sale within the shorter time frame.
The KLSE asked for estimates of time required for changes to firms' present computer systems to control the processes for the shortened settlement period.
It requested replies to be sent to the KLSE's Securities Clearing Automated Network Services Sdn Bhd unit by September 16.
